//buildCommand: Stated here rather than left to Railway, and stated with `npm install`
`npm ci` deletes node_modules before installing — that is what it is for.
Railway mounts a build cache at /app/node_modules/.cache, and a mount
point cannot be removed by the process it is mounted into, so every build
npm error EBUSY: resource busy or locked,
`npm install` installs into the existing directory and leaves the mount
alone. package-lock.json is committed and agrees with package.json, so
the resolved tree is the same one; what is given up is `ci`'s guarantee
that it *must* match. Commit a dependency change together with its
lockfile change and the two stay in step.
Config-as-code takes precedence over the dashboard, so this also
overrides any Build Command typed into the Railway UI — which is where
the failing `npm ci` was coming from.
build.buildCommand: npm install --no-audit --no-fund && npx prisma generate && npm run build

//startCommand: Stated here for the same reason the build command is: a Start Command
typed into the Railway dashboard overrides package.json, and one was.
The symptom was a working sign-in page that could not sign anyone in:
The table `main.LoginEvent` does not exist in the current database.
`prisma migrate deploy` is part of `npm start` precisely so that every
boot brings the database up to the schema the code expects. A start
command of just `tsx server.ts` skips it, so the volume held an empty
SQLite file and every query failed against a database with no tables.
